'''''Electronic Book Review''''' (''ebr'') is a peer-reviewed scholarly journal with emphasis on the digital. Founded in 1995 by [[Joseph Tabbi]] and [[Mark Amerika]], the journal was one of the first to devote a lasting web presence to the discussion of literature, theory, criticism, and the arts.

==Overview==
Since its inception, ''ebr'' has highlighted works characterized by innovation, resistance to genre, and creative use of emerging (electronic and web-specific) media. In 1996, ''[[Details (magazine)|Details]]'' referred to the journal as "a new mecca for cutting-edge fiction and criticism."<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Spillman|first1=Rob|title=Bibliofiles: Web crawling for bookworms|journal=Details|date=December 1996|issue=December 1996|page=144}}</ref> Initially managed in DIY fashion by contributing writers and programmers, by 1997 Anne Burdick joined the staff as design director, later bringing on Ewan Branda for the redesign.<ref>{{cite web|last1 = Hunter|first1 = Allison|url = http://www.allisonhunter.com/art/howarticle.html|website = How Magazine|publisher = How Magazine|accessdate = 10 September 2015|title = Weaving the Web}}</ref> Writing in ''Deep Sites: Intelligent Innovation in Contemporary Web Design'', Max Bruinsma characterizes ''ebr'' as "an interesting web of critical debates on electronic textuality, cyberculture, and the value of digital design literacy for scholarship and critical writing on the web."<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bruinsma|first1=Max|title=Deep Sites: Intelligent Innovation in Contemporary Web Design|date=2003|publisher=Thames and Hudson|location=New York|isbn=9780500283844|page=[https://archive.org/details/deepsitesintelli00brui/page/143 143]|url=https://archive.org/details/deepsitesintelli00brui/page/143}}</ref> Its emphasis on the materiality of text extended to early experiments with form on the site itself, including "glosses," in which comments by a guest curator appear embedded in existing articles, and the "weave" function, which allowed for fluid rearrangement of content "like a virtual loom that weaves different patterns each time you choose a different perspective."<ref>{{cite book|last1=Bruinsma|first1=Max|title=Deep Sites: Intelligent Innovation in Contemporary Web Design|date=2003|publisher=Thames and Hudson|location=New York|isbn=9780500283844|page=[https://archive.org/details/deepsitesintelli00brui/page/143 143]|url=https://archive.org/details/deepsitesintelli00brui/page/143}}</ref>

''ebr'' has received institutional support or affiliation from University of Illinois at Chicago,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Electronic Book Review (ebr) - Digital Humanities @ UIC|url = http://dh.uic.edu/2015/04/29/electronic-book-review-ebr/|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> The Center for Literary Computing at West Virginia University,<ref>{{Cite web|title = WVU to host prestigious web-based, peer-reviewed journal|url = http://wvutoday.wvu.edu/n/2012/04/17/wvu-to-host-prestigious-web-based-peer-reviewed-journal|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> University of Colorado at Boulder,<ref>{{Cite web|title = CU-Boulder A to Z {{!}} University of Colorado Boulder|url = http://www.colorado.edu/atoz/show/u19ec8aecba5ecf5604c0817cf9ce056c|website = www.colorado.edu|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> the Department of English, Art Center College of Design at Pasadena,<ref>{{Cite web|title = About EBR {{!}} Electronic Book Review|url = http://www.electronicbookreview.com/about|website = www.electronicbookreview.com|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> University of Stavanger,<ref>{{Cite web|title = University of Stavanger - Norway - Electronic Book Review|url = http://www.uis.no/library/scientific-literature/books/electronic-book-review-article89915-9252.html|website = www.uis.no|accessdate = 2015-09-25|archive-date = September 25, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150925163243/http://www.uis.no/library/scientific-literature/books/electronic-book-review-article89915-9252.html|url-status = dead}}</ref> the [[Electronic Literature Organization]],<ref>{{Cite web|title = Partners {{!}} Electronic Literature Organization|url = http://eliterature.org/partners/|website = eliterature.org|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> and the [[Consortium on Electronic Literature]] (CELL).<ref>{{Cite web|title = Electronic Book Review {{!}} CELL Project|url = http://cellproject.net/member-organization/electronic-book-review|website = cellproject.net|accessdate = 2015-09-25}}</ref> ''ebr'' is currently [[Editor-in-chief|edited]] by [[Joseph Tabbi]], among other scholars, critics, and artists on its Executive Board, including Anna Nacher (since 2023), Will Luers (since 2017), and [[Lai-Tze Fan]] (since 2017).

==Books and collaboration==
In conjunction with a trilogy of essay collections from MIT Press, ''ebr'' published a thread reproducing a portion of the essays while also expanding, critiquing, and responding to the print content. The "First Person" thread<ref>{{cite web|title=First Person|url=http://www.electronicbookreview.com/thread/firstperson|website=Electronic Book Review|access-date=November 4, 2015|archive-date=November 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151128080437/http://www.electronicbookreview.com/thread/firstperson/|url-status=dead}}</ref> exists as an accompaniment to the collections ''First Person: New Media as Story, Performance, and Game'', ''Second Person: Role-Playing and Story in Games and Playable Media'', and ''Third Person: Authoring and Exploring Vast Narratives'' by Pat Harrigan and Noah Wardrip-Fruin.
